Apple___Apple_scab.title: Apple scab
Apple___Apple_scab.tip: Remove fallen leaves and prune for airflow. Neem oil or a sulphur spray early in the season helps; ask your local agri extension about fungicides for severe cases.

Apple___Black_rot.title: Apple black rot
Apple___Black_rot.tip: Cut out dead bark and mummified fruit, and destroy them away from the tree. Improve air circulation by pruning; treat early with a recommended orchard fungicide.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.title: Cedar apple rust
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.tip: Remove nearby juniper or cedar hosts if practical, and clear fallen leaves. Preventive fungicide sprays at bud break work best; curative sprays do little.

Apple___healthy.title: Healthy apple leaf
Apple___healthy.tip: Leaf looks healthy. Keep up balanced watering, mulch around the base, and scout weekly so any problem is caught early.

Blueberry___healthy.title: Healthy blueberry leaf
Blueberry___healthy.tip: Leaf looks healthy. Blueberries like acidic soil and steady moisture; keep mulch topped up and avoid waterlogging.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.title: Healthy cherry leaf
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.tip: Leaf looks healthy. Maintain open canopy pruning and clean up fallen fruit to keep diseases away.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.title: Cherry powdery mildew
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.tip: Improve airflow and avoid wetting leaves when watering. Potassium bicarbonate or neem sprays check mild cases; remove badly coated shoots.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.title: Maize gray leaf spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.tip: Rotate crops and plough crop residue under after harvest. Choose tolerant hybrids next season; fungicide is worthwhile only if spots spread fast before grain fill.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.title: Maize common rust
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.tip: Usually cosmetic on tolerant hybrids and needs no action. If pustules cover most leaves early in the season, ask your extension officer about a fungicide spray.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.title: Healthy maize leaf
Corn_(maize)___healthy.tip: Leaf looks healthy. Keep nitrogen balanced and watch the whorl and lower leaves, where most maize diseases start.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.title: Maize northern leaf blight
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.tip: Bury or remove infected residue and rotate away from maize next season. Plant resistant hybrids; spray only if long lesions spread rapidly in wet weather.

Grape___Black_rot.title: Grape black rot
Grape___Black_rot.tip: Remove mummified berries and infected shoots promptly. Keep the canopy open so clusters dry fast; protectant sprays from bloom to bunch closure are key.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).title: Grape esca (black measles)
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).tip: No cure once wood is infected. Mark weak vines, prune late with clean tools, and replant dead vines with certified clean stock.

Grape___healthy.title: Healthy grape leaf
Grape___healthy.tip: Leaf looks healthy. Keep shoots tucked and thinned so clusters get light and air, and scout after rains.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.title: Grape leaf blight
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.tip: Clear fallen leaves and avoid overhead irrigation. Copper-based sprays used for downy mildew usually check this too.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).title: Citrus greening (HLB)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).tip: Serious bacterial disease spread by psyllid insects. Control psyllids, remove confirmed infected trees to protect neighbours, and report to your agriculture department.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.title: Peach bacterial spot
Peach___Bacterial_spot.tip: Avoid overhead watering and do not work among wet trees. Copper sprays early season plus resistant varieties are the main defences.

Peach___healthy.title: Healthy peach leaf
Peach___healthy.tip: Leaf looks healthy. Prune for an open vase shape and thin fruit so branches stay strong and airy.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.title: Pepper bacterial spot
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.tip: Use clean seed and seedlings, avoid handling wet plants, and mulch to stop soil splash. Copper sprays slow spread but will not cure spotted leaves.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.title: Healthy pepper leaf
Pepper,_bell___healthy.tip: Leaf looks healthy. Water at the base, mulch well, and watch young leaves where sucking pests first appear.

Potato___Early_blight.title: Potato early blight
Potato___Early_blight.tip: Water at soil level and mulch to stop splash. Remove lowest affected leaves; protectant sprays (mancozeb or chlorothalonil type) help in wet seasons.

Potato___healthy.title: Healthy potato leaf
Potato___healthy.tip: Leaf looks healthy. Hill soil around stems and keep foliage dry late in the day to prevent blight.

Potato___Late_blight.title: Potato late blight
Potato___Late_blight.tip: Act fast: destroy affected foliage, stop irrigation, and harvest early if spread is rapid. Preventive sprays before rainy spells are far more effective than late ones.

Raspberry___healthy.title: Healthy raspberry leaf
Raspberry___healthy.tip: Leaf looks healthy. Keep rows narrow, remove old canes after fruiting, and keep fruit off the ground.

Soybean___healthy.title: Healthy soybean leaf
Soybean___healthy.tip: Leaf looks healthy. Rotate with cereals and avoid working the field when plants are wet.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.title: Squash powdery mildew
Squash___Powdery_mildew.tip: Plant in full sun with wide spacing. Milk-water or potassium bicarbonate sprays suppress early coatings; remove the worst leaves first.

Strawberry___healthy.title: Healthy strawberry leaf
Strawberry___healthy.tip: Leaf looks healthy. Straw mulch under berries, drip watering, and yearly bed renewal keep plants productive.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.title: Strawberry leaf scorch
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.tip: Remove scorched older leaves and renovate beds after harvest. Keep plants vigorous with steady water; severe beds are best replanted with certified stock.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.title: Tomato bacterial spot
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.tip: Stake plants, mulch, and water the soil, not the leaves. Start with disease-free seed; copper sprays only limit new infections.

Tomato___Early_blight.title: Tomato early blight
Tomato___Early_blight.tip: Mulch and bottom-water to stop soil splash on lower leaves. Strip the lowest affected leaves and apply a protectant spray in humid weather.

Tomato___Late_blight.title: Tomato late blight
Tomato___Late_blight.tip: Destroy affected plants fast (do not compost) and protect neighbours with preventive spray. Choose resistant varieties next planting.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.title: Tomato leaf mold
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.tip: A greenhouse problem from high humidity: ventilate, space plants, and water mornings only. Resistant varieties solve it permanently.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.title: Tomato septoria leaf spot
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.tip: Remove lower spotted leaves and mulch heavily. Rotate beds yearly; protectant sprays work if started before spots climb the plant.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.title: Tomato spider mites
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.tip: Look for fine webbing under leaves. Blast plants with water, encourage ladybirds, and use neem or miticidal soap; avoid broad insecticides that kill mite predators.

Tomato___Target_Spot.title: Tomato target spot
Tomato___Target_Spot.tip: Same care as early blight: airflow, mulching, lower-leaf removal. Fungicide sprays registered for early blight generally cover this too.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.title: Tomato mosaic virus
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.tip: No cure: pull and destroy infected plants, disinfect tools and hands, and do not smoke near tomatoes. Use resistant varieties and certified seed next time.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.title: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.tip: Spread by whiteflies: use insect-proof nursery netting and control whiteflies early. Remove infected seedlings immediately; resistant varieties are the best defence.

Tomato___healthy.title: Healthy tomato leaf
Tomato___healthy.tip: Leaf looks healthy. Stake, prune suckers lightly for airflow, and water the base consistently to avoid blossom-end rot.
